$comment: THE PROVIDERS THIS ENGINE KNOWS. Data, not code: preflight validates a PRD's aiProvider against `known`, and nothing in the pipeline carries a vendor name as a literal. Adding a provider is an edit here and nowhere else. Extracted from preflight-check.sh on 2026-08-16, where the same set lived as a Python set literal inside an embedded program — a place no other check could read and no one would think to update.
$effortBadgeComment: Providers whose viewer badge is driven by the effort tier, so effort=low renders as the cheapest badge. Preflight warns when a story on one of these is assigned effort=low, because the badge then misreports the model actually doing the work.
$modelRulesComment: Per-provider rules about the MODEL a story may be assigned. `requiresSlug` means the model must be a routed slug carrying a '/' — an assignment without one names a model the router cannot reach, and the story fails with an empty result rather than a routing error. `knownModels` is advisory: an unlisted model warns, because a new model appearing is normal and a typo looks the same. Absent from this map means no rule.

minimax.$suitabilityComment: Test-authoring drifted on this provider (see the brownfield test-authoring incident): it rewrites the assertions instead of writing the test the criterion asks for. A story whose files are test files must not be assigned to it.

$statusComment: The story statuses a PRD may carry. Preflight rejects anything else — an unexpected status is read as not-completed by every gate, so a typo silently fails a story that succeeded.
